_meta.purpose: Comprehensive GitOps SOP and reference matrix for AI Agents generating Hybrid Gitmoji/Conventional Commits, calculating SemVer bumps, generating Changelogs, and handling Releases.
_meta.enforcement: MANDATORY: Agents MUST ingest these rules and use the embedded matrices for all version control operations to prevent malformed history and corrupted file syntaxes. SemVer and changelog classification MUST be derived from the exact selected intent rows, not broad Conventional Commit cc_type categories.

rules: The <subject> MUST be imperative, present tense (e.g., 'change' not 'changed' or 'changes').
The <subject> MUST NOT end with a period.
The total length of the subject line MUST NOT exceed 72 characters.
If the diff includes breaking changes, append '!' after the scope: `<emoji> <cc_type>(<scope>)!: <subject>`.

semver_specification.faq_rules: v0.x.x is for initial development; the public API should not be considered stable. v1.0.0 defines the public API.

version_injection_matrix.enforcement: When tasked with versioning a standalone file, the agent MUST use the syntax mapped to the file extension. NEVER inject comments into unsupported formats like JSON. Default to project-level files (e.g., package.json, VERSION) unless executing on a standalone script.

json.rule: DO NOT use comments. Find or create a `version` key at the root object level.

hash_comment.rule: Inject or replace on line 1 or 2 of the file.

slash_comment.rule: Inject or replace on line 1 or 2 of the file.

block_comment.rule: Inject or replace at the top of the document.

agentic_commit_workflow.philosophy: Traceable, machine-readable, and visually clear history. Never hallucinate intent.
phases: Phase 1: Diff Analysis. Execute `git diff` to identify the exact files changed and the nature of the logic altered.
Phase 2: Intent Classification. Determine the PRIMARY intent of the commit. Does it add a feature, fix a bug, or merely refactor?
Phase 3: Matrix Query. Query the `gitmoji_reference_matrix` and select the single most appropriate object based on the `description`.
Phase 4: Subject Line Generation. Format strictly according to `specifications_and_standards.commit_format.syntax`.
Phase 5: Body Generation. If the diff is complex, leave a blank line after the subject and write a detailed body explaining 'Why' and 'What'.
Phase 6: Commit Execution. Execute the commit.

agentic_release_workflow.philosophy: Automated, deterministic releases based on semantic commit history and exact SOP intent-row metadata.
phases: Phase 1: Log Parsing. Read the git commit history since the last SemVer tag. Parse each commit header and, when present, structured secondary intent metadata from `Included changes` and machine-readable trailers.

Phase 2: SemVer Calculation. Evaluate the exact `semver_impact` values from the selected primary and secondary SOP intent rows. The highest impact (MAJOR > MINOR > PATCH > NONE) dictates the bump. Do not infer SemVer impact from broad `cc_type` categories alone.

Phase 3: Target Resolution. Identify the canonical files that receive the version bump (e.g., `pyproject.toml`, `package.json`, `VERSION`, or standalone scripts) according to the release configuration.
Phase 4: File Injection. Use the `version_injection_matrix` and the `semver_regex` to safely find, insert, or update version strings in target files without corrupting syntax.

Phase 5: Changelog Generation. Follow `changelog_generation_rules` to parse primary and secondary commit intents, group them by each selected row's `changelog_group`, and prepend the generated release notes to CHANGELOG.md.

Phase 6: Tag & Release. Commit the version and changelog updates using 🔖 (`:bookmark:`). Create an annotated git tag (`git tag -a v<VERSION> -m 'Release v<VERSION>'`). Suggest or execute the forge CLI command (e.g., `gh release create`) to push the tag and release notes.

changelog_generation_rules.enforcement: Do not dump a raw git log. Parse the hybrid commits and group them under markdown headers based on the `changelog_group` mapped in the reference matrix.
taxonomy: Changed: for changes in existing functionality (e.g., ♻️ refactor, 🎨 style).
Fixed: for any bug fixes (e.g., 🐛 fix).
Miscellaneous: for chores, docs, and build updates (e.g., 📝 docs, 🚀 chore).

semver_resolution_matrix.MAJOR: Triggered by explicit breaking-change syntax, a BREAKING CHANGE footer, or any selected primary or secondary intent row whose semver_impact is MAJOR.
semver_resolution_matrix.MINOR: Triggered by any selected primary or secondary intent row whose semver_impact is MINOR, unless a MAJOR rule applies.
semver_resolution_matrix.PATCH: Triggered by any selected primary or secondary intent row whose semver_impact is PATCH, unless a MAJOR or MINOR rule applies.
semver_resolution_matrix.NONE: Applied only when all selected primary and secondary intent rows have semver_impact NONE.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change improves formatting or code structure without changing runtime behaviour.
Use when the dominant user-visible or operational impact is improved speed, latency, throughput, or resource usage.
Use when the primary change actively removes code or files. Prefer ⚰️ for dead-code removal and 🗑️ for deprecation.
Use for a normal bug fix where the primary change corrects incorrect runtime behaviour.
Use only for urgent high-impact fixes, especially production breakages or critical regressions.
Use when the primary change adds a new user-facing or API-visible capability. Prefer more specific feature intents when applicable.
Use for documentation-only or documentation-primary changes. Do not use when functional security, build, runtime, or release changes are the main impact.
Use when the primary change is deployment-related. Prefer 👷 for CI build system and 🔖 for release/version tags.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add or update the UI and style files
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change updates UI styling or visual presentation. Prefer ♿️ for accessibility-driven changes.
Use only for initial project creation or major bootstrap commits.
Use when the primary change is adding or updating tests. Prefer 🧪 for intentionally adding a failing test.
Use when the primary change fixes a security or privacy issue. Security fixes should not be hidden under docs/chore headers.
Use for secret-management changes, encrypted secret metadata, or credential orchestration. Do not use for plaintext secrets; those should be blocked.
Use for release commits, version tags, and release metadata. Prefer dependency/build intents for dependency-only version changes.
Use when the primary change fixes compiler, linter, or static-analysis warnings. Prefer 🎨 for pure formatting.
Use sparingly for temporary work-in-progress commits. Avoid in polished public history.
Use when the primary change fixes a failing CI/build pipeline. Prefer 👷 for adding or updating CI systems.
Use when the primary change downgrades one or more dependencies.
Use when the primary change upgrades existing dependencies.
Use when the primary change pins dependency versions or tightens version constraints.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add or update CI build system
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use for adding or updating CI/build automation. Prefer 💚 when fixing a broken CI build.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add or update analytics or track code
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change adds or updates analytics, telemetry, tracking, or metrics collection.
Use for internal restructuring, centralisation, or deduplication when no more specific refactor subtype dominates.
Use when the primary change adds a new dependency or tool dependency.
Use when the primary change removes a dependency or tool dependency.
Use for configuration-file changes. Do not use when code merely reads config; choose the code intent instead.
Use when the primary change adds or updates local development scripts or task-runner commands.
Use when the primary change adds or updates internationalisation/localisation support.
Use for typo/spelling/grammar corrections, especially in documentation. Prefer 📝 for substantial documentation updates.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Write bad code that needs to be improved
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use only when the author intentionally marks the change as bad/temporary technical debt. Avoid in public polished history.
Use when the primary change reverts or rolls back previous changes.
Use for actual merge commits or branch integrations. Normal feature/fix commits should not use this.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add or update compiled files or packages
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change affects packaging, build artifacts, package data, or distribution metadata.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Update code due to external API changes
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change adapts code to an external API or third-party contract change.
Use only when the primary change is moving or renaming files/resources. Do not use for general centralisation, modularisation, or portability improvements unless file movement is dominant.
Use when the primary change adds or updates license, copyright, or legal notice files.
Use when the primary change is backwards-incompatible or explicitly declares a breaking change. Breaking changes must not be hidden under lower-priority headers.
Use when the primary change adds or updates assets such as images, media, or static files.
Use when the primary change improves accessibility. Prefer this over generic feature or style when accessibility is the intent.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add or update comments in source code
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change adds or updates comments/docstrings in source code without changing behaviour.
Use only for explicit joke/informal commits. Avoid in public project history.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add or update text and literals
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change updates user-facing text or literals. Prefer 🌐 for localization/i18n changes.
Use when the primary change affects database schema, migrations, queries, or persistence behaviour.
Use when the primary change adds or updates logging. Prefer 📈 for analytics/tracking telemetry.
Use when the primary change removes or silences logs. Prefer 🔒️ if the change removes sensitive logging for security/privacy.
Use when the primary change updates contributor, maintainer, or acknowledgement metadata.
Use when the primary change improves end-user experience or usability without introducing a major new feature.
Use for broad architectural restructuring. Do not use for small helper extraction or ordinary internal refactoring.
Use when the primary change improves responsive/mobile design.
Use when the primary change adds or updates mocks, stubs, fakes, or test doubles.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add or update an easter egg
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use only when the primary change is an easter egg or hidden novelty behaviour.
Use when the primary change updates `.gitignore` or VCS ignore patterns.
Use when the primary change adds or updates test snapshots or golden files.
Use when the primary change is experimental or exploratory. Prefer ✨ for production-ready features.
Use when the primary change improves search engine optimization.
Use when the primary change adds or updates types, typing models, schemas, or annotations.
Use when the primary change adds or updates seed data files.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add, update, or remove feature flags
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change adds, updates, or removes feature flags or runtime toggles.
Use when the primary change catches, handles, or recovers from errors. Prefer 🦺 for validation-specific changes.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add or update animations and transitions
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change adds or updates animations, transitions, or motion effects.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Deprecate code that needs to be cleaned up
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change marks code or APIs as deprecated. Prefer 🔥 or ⚰️ when code is actually removed.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Work on code related to authorization, roles and permissions
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change adds or updates authorization, roles, permissions, or access-control features.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Simple fix for a non-critical issue
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use for small non-critical fixes. Prefer 🐛 for normal bugs and 🚑 for critical hotfixes.
Use when the primary change adds or updates data exploration, inspection, or investigation artifacts.
Use when the primary change removes dead, unused, or unreachable code. Prefer 🔥 for broader active code/file removal.
Use when the primary change intentionally adds a failing or expected-failure test.
Use when the primary change adds or updates business/domain logic.
Use when the primary change adds or updates application/service health checks.
Use when the primary change affects infrastructure, platform, or system-level runtime configuration.
Use when the primary change improves local developer or contributor experience.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add sponsorships or money related infrastructure
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change adds sponsorship, funding, billing, payment, or money-related infrastructure.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add or update code related to multithreading or concurrency
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change adds or updates threading, async, concurrency, or parallel execution behaviour.

gitmoji_reference_matrix.description: Add or update code related to validation
gitmoji_reference_matrix.selection_rule: Use when the primary change adds or hardens validation/safety guards. Prefer 🥅 for error-catching and 🏷️ for type-only changes.
Use when the primary change improves offline support or offline-first behaviour.
Use when the primary change preserves or adds backwards compatibility.
